summary: Preserve integrated legacy refs during first native allocation

delivery.outcome: Permit first native bootstrap allocation in the presence of preserved, demonstrably integrated historical ticket refs, without deleting branches, taking over active ownership or relaxing exact installer-byte acknowledgement and external fenced edit admission. Publish the material fix and atomic package/version projections.
nonGoals: No changes in the separate blocked ticket-341 adoption-allocation-plan worktree
No deletion, reset or movement of historical branches or worktrees
No bypass of external repository-admission policy, required CI or independent Validator approval

architecture.decision: Replace the unconditional historical ticket-ref refusal with a bounded, independently recomputed Git containment observation. Preserve all refs and report them as historical context only when exact base containment is demonstrated; retain refusal for non-contained or unreadable refs, existing native reservations/tickets, additional worktrees, changed installer bytes, stale state and conflicting live ownership. The controller separately grants the exact write scope; observation never grants editing, deletion, review or merge. Add real-Git regression fixtures and publish an atomic standard patch release.
interfaceChanges: Proof-aware historical ref observation during first bootstrap acknowledgement
architecture.rollback: Keep the previous published package; candidate activation and source revert use the existing independent publisher. Preserve bootstrap snapshots and all target branches.

validation.evidence: Real Git fixtures preserve exact historical refs and reject active, non-contained, stale or unreadable state
Scoped checks, required protected CI, independent exact-head source publication and final package release proof
